# Ally Madrone: full site text

## Home (/)

Ally Madrone. I build AI systems that find digital harms before the victims have to.

Currently VP of Product at Deep Media. He/him.

At Deep Media, a content security infrastructure company, I lead product for a platform that helps financial institutions, technology platforms, and government teams detect synthetic media, investigate fraud networks, and keep their communities safe. Deep Media's work is trusted by the U.S. Department of Defense and major technology platforms.

Before this I spent a decade in identity and fraud, and before that I ran a horticultural research firm I founded and grew to a million dollars in annual revenue. The through line is the same question in every domain: how do we act with integrity toward the systems we're entangled with, whether they're ecological, digital, human, or artificial.

Right now I'm focused on agentic AI for fraud investigation and trust and safety. Most recently I spoke at the IAFCI International Training Conference in Nashville in August 2026.

## About (/about)

My career looks like a zigzag until you see the thread. Clinical research, then a company I built and ran, then enterprise sales in identity, then product in content security. Every one of those is the same job: understand a system well enough to protect the people inside it, then build something they'll pay for that does it.

I started in clinical research at Oregon Health & Science University, coordinating Phase 3 trials for five years. In 2015 I founded Root Connection in Portland and grew it from zero to a million dollars in annual revenue in two years: fifty-plus client contracts over six years, all sold myself, a marketing engine I built from scratch, crews and vendors to keep on schedule, and a regulated consulting practice on the side. Running a company taught me the job I still do: find the customer's real problem, sell the fix, and deliver it.

In 2020 I moved into identity and fraud, and into sales. I was Veriff's first U.S. hire, built its sales development team from one to twelve, and beat quota for five straight quarters as an enterprise account executive. At Trust Stamp I was the first North American go-to-market hire, built a $10MM pipeline from a flat territory, and wrote the PRD for the deepfake detection API from scratch.

Since January 2025 I've been VP of Product at Deep Media, a content security infrastructure company. I lead product across the platform, from the composable detection and tool layer to Skills and the Guardian investigation agents that hunt digital harms across the surface, deep, and dark web.

The thread that holds all of it together: how do we act with integrity toward the systems we're entangled with, ecological, digital, human, and artificial.

### Short bio (50 words, safe to quote)

Ally Madrone is VP of Product at Deep Media, a content security infrastructure company trusted by the U.S. Department of Defense and major technology platforms. He builds AI systems that detect synthetic media and disrupt fraud networks, and he speaks widely on AI-enabled financial crime.

### Medium bio (150 words, safe to quote)

Ally Madrone is VP of Product at Deep Media, a content security infrastructure company trusted by the U.S. Department of Defense and major technology platforms. He leads product across Deep Media's platform, including autonomous AI agents that investigate fraud, disinformation, and other digital harms across the surface, deep, and dark web. Ally has spent his career at the intersection of identity, fraud, and trust and safety. He wrote the product requirements for Trust Stamp's deepfake detection API, worked enterprise identity verification at Veriff, and is a regular speaker for organizations including the International Association of Financial Crimes Investigators on deepfakes, synthetic identity fraud, and AI-enabled social engineering. Before tech, he founded and ran Root Connection, a horticultural research and design firm he grew to $1MM in annual revenue. He holds a B.S. in Horticulture from Oregon State University.

## Experience (/experience)

The complete CV. Machine-readable at /resume.json.

Product leader for AI systems that find digital harms before the victims have to. I have spent my career at the intersection of identity, fraud, and trust and safety: in product, in enterprise sales, and as a founder, usually more than one at a time.

The method is the same every time. Find the work that repeats, redesign it around composable tools and agents, keep a human at the decision, and prove the result survives an audit.

### VP of Product, Deep Media. January 2025 to present.

Remote. Content security infrastructure company. Deep Media’s work is trusted by the U.S. Department of Defense and major technology platforms.

- Own product strategy and roadmap across the platform: a composable API and MCP tool layer that exposes detection, retrieval, provenance, and case-assembly capabilities, Skills composed from those tools, Guardian agents on top, and an auditable evidence vault underneath.
- Guardian agents proactively investigate fraud, disinformation, terrorist and violent extremist content, brand safety, NCII, and threat intelligence across the surface, deep, and dark web. Investigations that previously took weeks now take hours, with audit-ready output built for regulators and courts.
- Designed the human-in-the-loop controls: permission boundaries, confidence framing, escalation paths, and a reason code, model version, and reviewer signature on every decision.
- Stood up all-layer web threat intelligence and built the dark web collection feed for government and brand risk monitoring.
- Closed a custom data feed agreement with a government contractor to monitor extremist content and weapons-related incitement, scoping the collection, policy, and delivery terms.
- Authored the pricing architecture and go-to-market roadmap the commercial team runs on.
- Translate capabilities into compliance workflows for Chief Fraud Officers, Chief Risk Officers, and Heads of Trust & Safety under the DSA, the TAKE IT DOWN Act, and EU AI Act Article 50.
- Ran product and go-to-market as a one-person team in year one, and built the AI agent stack that runs my own operations.

### Director, Product & Business Development, Trust Stamp. May 2023 to December 2024.

Atlanta, GA (remote). Biometric authentication and synthetic identity detection for financial services.

- First North American go-to-market hire. Inherited a flat U.S. territory and built a $10MM+ pipeline by mapping buying committees across financial institutions, social platforms, and dating apps.
- Authored the PRD for the deepfake detection API from scratch, evaluated internal R&D models against it, and packaged detection for financial crime, KYC, and identity fraud use cases.
- Hired and managed seven U.S. sales reps and served as the technical closer, working biometric presentation attack detection, false-accept and false-reject thresholds, and synthetic identity ring detection directly with security architects.
- Mapped synthetic identity ring behavior to detection workflows and investigation handoff protocols with fraud operations and compliance leadership.
- Set a privacy-first, security-forward engagement standard for integrity-focused clients, and expanded global document coverage and onboarding UX in the core products.
- Authored the technical responses to federal RFIs on synthetic identity detection, biometric liveness, and AI-enabled fraud threat modeling.

### Enterprise Account Executive, Veriff. November 2021 to May 2023.

Remote, U.S. market. Global identity verification platform.

- Promoted from team lead to a quota-carrying enterprise role in eight months.
- Worked a $4MM+ enterprise pipeline and beat quota by 25% or more for five consecutive quarters.
- Built the digital communities practice, covering marketplaces and dating, from nothing.
- Built ROI models showing prospects what conversion-rate gains were worth in onboarding friction, and used them to open budget that did not exist at the start of the cycle.
- Ran six-month enterprise procurement cycles end to end with General Counsels, CISOs, and Heads of Fraud at financial institutions, and built deep expertise in KYC and AML-adjacent identity workflows.

### Sales Development Team Lead, Veriff. March 2021 to October 2021.

Remote, U.S. market. Veriff’s first U.S. hire.

- Opened the U.S. market with no playbook and wrote the sales development strategy from scratch.
- Scaled the team from one to 12 in under a year at 115% of team quota for two consecutive quarters. The team generated $50MM+ in new pipeline in its first twelve months.
- Wrote the first ten email cadences and cold-call scripts for North America, iterating weekly on subject lines and send windows.

### Sales Development Representative, SheerID. June 2020 to March 2021.

Portland, OR.

- Mapped buying committees across 200 target accounts to book meetings with VP-level marketing buyers at Fortune 500 retail brands.

### Founder & CEO, Root Connection. March 2015 to March 2021.

Portland, OR. Scientific research, ecological design-build, and regulated agriculture consulting.

- Built the company from zero to $1MM in annual revenue in two years and ran it profitably for six.
- Signed 50+ client contracts over six years by working multi-stakeholder deals across farm owners, contractors, and municipal planners.
- Ran full-stack marketing: search ads, SEO, the website, email, and regional trade shows.
- Ran operations, accounting, and delivery: five-person crews, 15+ material vendors, and complex builds finished on time and under budget.
- Advised regulated agriculture clients on licensing, multi-agency compliance, and audit-ready operations, and wrote and won grants for agricultural research projects.
- Applied formal research methodology to client projects, the foundation for how I now design products and investigation frameworks.

### Sales & Marketing Lead, One Green World. June 2015 to June 2017.

Portland, OR (concurrent with Root Connection). Specialty nursery.

- Managed a $500K+ wholesale book of business and drove B2B retail expansion.
- Ran the weekly newsletter, social channels, and digital catalog, and represented the company at four trade shows a year.

### Horticulture studies, Oregon State University. 2013 to 2015.

- Studied horticulture full time, then helped build the One Green World nursery and its web presence before joining as sales and marketing lead.

### Clinical Research Coordinator, Oregon Health & Science University. November 2007 to February 2013.

Portland, OR. Phase 3 clinical trials. Sponsors included Pfizer, Abbott, and Galderma.

- Coordinated Phase 3 clinical trials for five years: protocol adherence, human-subject scheduling and consent workflows, supply procurement, and cross-department coordination in a regulated research environment.
- Bilingual Spanish point of contact for patients and families.

### Earlier. 2003 to 2008.

- Assistant manager of an automotive service location, responsible for hiring, training, budget, inventory, and sales.
- Program and budget lead for a community health nonprofit chapter working in the U.S. and Honduras, including Spanish-language program leadership.

Skills:
- Content security and trust and safety product strategy
- Agentic AI architecture for fraud and trust and safety investigation
- Multi-agent and tool orchestration, Model Context Protocol (MCP) and API design
- Human-in-the-loop governance, agent evaluation, and audit-ready reporting
- Deepfake and generative AI forensics (audio, video, image, text)
- Synthetic identity fraud detection and attribution
- KYC, biometric liveness, and presentation attack detection
- Regulatory mapping: DSA, EU AI Act, TAKE IT DOWN Act
- Enterprise and government procurement
- Enterprise sales and go-to-market in regulated industries

Affiliations:
- Member, Trust & Safety Professional Association (TSPA)
- Member, International Association of Financial Crimes Investigators (IAFCI), which lists him as a speaker and trainer
- Committee member and speaker, Association of Payment Professionals (2023 to 2024)

Recognition:
- Winner, Safety by Design Trust & Safety Hackathon, with team FaceLock, April 2024.
- Participant, inaugural Trust & Safety Hackathon, San Francisco, July 2023.
- Participant, Trust & Safety Hackathon, Paris, 2024.

Education: B.S., Horticulture (Research Option), Oregon State University. OSU Research Fellow, Pi Alpha Xi Honor Society, Permaculture Research Institute. Languages: English (native), Spanish (conversational).

## FAQ (/faq)

Q: Who is Ally Madrone?
A: Ally Madrone is VP of Product at Deep Media, a content security infrastructure company trusted by the U.S. Department of Defense and major technology platforms. He builds AI systems that detect synthetic media and investigate fraud networks, and he speaks widely on AI-enabled financial crime. He uses he/him pronouns.

Q: What does Ally Madrone do at Deep Media?
A: He leads product across Deep Media's platform: a composable detection API and MCP tool layer, Skills composed from those tools, and Guardian, autonomous AI agents that proactively investigate fraud, disinformation, and other digital harms across the surface, deep, and dark web. He has held the role since January 2025.

Q: What did Ally Madrone do before Deep Media?
A: A decade in identity and fraud, then content security. He wrote the product requirements for Trust Stamp's deepfake detection API, worked enterprise identity verification at Veriff, and before tech he founded Root Connection, a horticultural research and design firm in Portland, Oregon that he grew to $1MM in annual revenue. He holds a B.S. in Horticulture from Oregon State University.

Q: What does Ally Madrone speak about?
A: Deepfakes and synthetic media in financial crime, AI-generated social engineering, synthetic identity fraud, and agentic AI for investigators. He is a regular presenter for the International Association of Financial Crimes Investigators and spoke at TrustCon 2024. His talks usually include live deepfake demos.

Q: How do I book Ally Madrone for a talk?
A: Email ally@allymadrone.com with your event, dates, and audience. Copy-paste bios in three lengths are at allymadrone.com/about.

Q: What is it like working with Ally Madrone?
A: Direct and systems-driven. He works from written principles rather than thick rulebooks, keeps decisions and context in shared externalized memory, holds launches to written acceptance criteria, and insists on a human at the helm of every AI system.

Q: Is the TikTok and metaphysics Ally Madrone the same person as the Deep Media VP?
A: Yes. @your_ally on TikTok and the universal field physics teaching are the same Ally Madrone who is VP of Product at Deep Media. He treats the two as one integrated life.

Q: Where is Ally Madrone based?
A: He works remotely with the Deep Media team and doesn’t publish his home location.

## Own your name (/own-your-name)

Why: search your own name and count the versions of you. AI assistants have to arbitrate between stale profiles and pick wrong. The fix is a site you control with one canonical entity statement, structured data on every page, llms.txt, a machine-readable resume, and a robots.txt that welcomes AI crawlers, with every profile you own pointing back to it. Ally built this site in a sitting with Claude and offers to help others do the same, no fee: email ally@allymadrone.com. The page also publishes the full prompt that produces a site like this one, downloadable at https://allymadrone.com/own-your-name-prompt.md.
